steps.assert: This is the immediately-pre-write assertion against CURRENT main, not the historical bootstrap head that sequence 2 read. It closes the bootstrap-race gap: sequences 1-5 above prove repository identity, integration id, and ruleset/classic-protection state, but none of them re-reads the workflow definitions on main, so an intervening pull request that removed, renamed, or path-filtered a required workflow after the bootstrap merge would otherwise pass sequences 1-5 and only be discovered when sequence 8 or 11's required-context writes started failing every future pull request. Resolve current main's tip live from this same response (base_commit.sha for bootstrap_merge_sha, and the head commit of the comparison for current main); assert merge_base_commit.sha == bootstrap_merge_sha (bootstrap_merge_sha is an ancestor of current main; main was not rewritten), and assert the response's files array contains zero entries whose filename starts with any prefix in template_variables.protected_paths. A compare with zero commits ahead (current main == bootstrap_merge_sha) trivially satisfies this by returning an empty files array. This assertion, together with sequence 2's proof that bootstrap_merge_sha's predecessor head emitted all four contexts, is what proves current main can safely require all four contexts: the protected workflow bytes reviewed at bootstrap are proved byte-identical to what is on main right now, immediately before sequence 7's first write, not merely at some earlier historical instant.
steps.on_mismatch: stop before any write. If merge_base_commit.sha != bootstrap_merge_sha, main was rewritten since the bootstrap merge; treat as a governance incident, not routine drift. If any protected path appears in files, a governance-path change landed on main after the bootstrap merge without going through this document's write sequence; re-review current main's actual workflow/manifest state, capture a fresh bootstrap_merge_sha-equivalent baseline (or run the section 4 maintenance procedure if the change was legitimate maintenance), and re-run this preflight from sequence 1 before any write proceeds. Do not require a context whose current-main definition was not just proved identical to what was reviewed.

residual_risk: Every rule written here can be rewritten or deleted by the repository owner-admin, who is the accepted root of trust for this personal repository per DECISIONS.md D031. This apply document does not claim to prevent that; it makes the intended state explicit and machine-comparable, proves current main's protected-path bytes match what was reviewed immediately before the first write (sequence 6), and lets scripts/fork-health.sh --live and the governance fixtures detect any later drift.
